Επιτρέπεται η ελεύθερη χρήση του υλικού µε αναφορά στην πηγή προέλευσής του.
thought_title: Condemnation of those who disturb the church
orientation: Cyril is closing his fragment by condemning those who disturb the church and its Christ-loving people, and he appears to be stating that he considers them condemned, with a broken phrase about natures and forms.
pass_a_gloss: [damaged] ... I consider [them] to have been condemned; for of natures and of forms ...

choices.why: The verb is restored from the context of the fragment's first-person voice; it expresses Cyril's judgment.
The perfect passive infinitive conveys a completed judgment against those who disturb the church.
The glossary specifies 'natures' for φυσεων, and the genitive plural fits the broken phrase.
The glossary specifies 'forms' for μορφων, and the genitive plural parallels φυσεων.

pass_b_english: I consider them to have been condemned, for of natures and of forms . . . [the papyrus breaks off]
notes: The source text is heavily damaged at the beginning of this section. Only the restored phrase 'ἡγου]μαι κατακεκρι[σθαι·] φυσεων γαρ και μ[ο]ρφων' is legible. The gloss reflects only the legible and restored text; no text has been invented beyond the bracketed restorations.
